description: 16-week marathon plan for runners with half marathon experience. Based on Hal Higdon Intermediate. Goal: Sub-4:00 marathon.

weeks.focusDescription: Foundation building - establish baseline aerobic fitness

days.cardioNotes: Easy conversational pace. Focus on form and breathing rhythm.

exercises.name: Goblet Squat
exercises.notes: Focus on depth and controlled descent

exercises.name: Romanian Deadlift
exercises.notes: Keep back flat, hinge at hips

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.notes: Each leg, focus on front leg drive

days.cardioNotes: Easy conversational pace. Keep it comfortable.
Steady effort. This builds midweek volume for marathon prep.
Complete rest or 30 min easy cycling/swimming if desired
Long slow distance. Stay conversational, focus on time on feet.

weeks.focusDescription: Building base aerobic capacity with slight volume increase

days.cardioNotes: Easy conversational pace.

exercises.name: Dead Bug
exercises.notes: 12 reps each side, slow and controlled

days.cardioNotes: Recovery pace, conversational.
Steady aerobic effort.
Complete rest or easy cross-training
Long slow distance. Build time on feet gradually.

weeks.focusDescription: Recovery week - reduce volume by 25% to absorb training

days.cardioNotes: Easy recovery pace. Enjoy the lighter week.
Keep it easy and relaxed.
Steady but comfortable.
Reduced long run for recovery. Keep it comfortable.

weeks.focusDescription: Resume volume progression with introduction to tempo work

days.cardioNotes: Easy conversational pace.
Recovery pace.
1 mile easy warm-up, 3 miles at comfortably hard tempo pace, 1 mile easy cool-down. Tempo should feel controlled but challenging.
Complete rest or easy cross-training
Long slow distance. Focus on steady effort.

weeks.focusDescription: Continue building base with quality tempo work

days.cardioNotes: Easy conversational pace.
Recovery pace, stay comfortable.
1 mile easy warm-up, 4 miles at tempo pace, 1 mile easy cool-down. Tempo pace should be comfortably hard.
Complete rest or easy cross-training
Long slow distance. Stay aerobic and comfortable.

weeks.focusDescription: Peak base building week before transitioning to marathon-specific phase

days.cardioNotes: Easy conversational pace.
Recovery pace.
1 mile easy warm-up, 4 miles at tempo pace, 1 mile easy cool-down.
Complete rest or easy cross-training
Longest run of base phase. Stay comfortable and aerobic.

weeks.focusDescription: Recovery week - reduce volume before marathon-specific build phase

days.cardioNotes: Easy recovery pace.
Keep it easy and relaxed.
Steady comfortable pace.
Reduced long run. Stay comfortable and enjoy the easier week.

weeks.focusDescription: Begin marathon-specific work with race pace segments

days.cardioNotes: Easy conversational pace.
Recovery pace.
1 mile easy warm-up, 6 miles at marathon goal pace, 2 miles easy cool-down. This is your first sustained marathon pace effort.
Complete rest or easy cross-training
Long slow distance. Building weekly long run back up after recovery week.

weeks.focusDescription: Continue building volume with marathon-specific work

days.cardioNotes: Easy conversational pace.
Recovery pace.
1 mile easy warm-up, 8 miles at marathon goal pace, 1 mile easy cool-down. Build confidence at race pace.
Complete rest or easy cross-training
Long slow distance. Maintain aerobic effort.

weeks.focusDescription: Peak building week with progression to 20-mile long run

days.cardioNotes: Easy conversational pace.
Recovery pace.
1 mile easy warm-up, 8 miles at marathon goal pace, 1 mile easy cool-down. Lock in race pace feel.
Complete rest or easy cross-training
Your first 20-miler. Stay comfortable and aerobic. Take walk breaks if needed. Practice race nutrition.

weeks.focusDescription: Recovery week after 20-miler - absorb training stress

days.cardioNotes: Easy recovery pace. Let legs recover from 20-miler.
Keep it easy and relaxed.
1 mile easy warm-up, 3 miles at tempo pace, 1 mile easy cool-down. Lighter quality work this week.
Reduced long run. Recovery week after peak volume.
Easy conversational pace.
Recovery pace.
1 mile easy warm-up, 10 miles at marathon goal pace, 1 mile easy cool-down. Longest marathon pace effort.
Complete rest or easy cross-training
Second 20-miler. Should feel more comfortable than the first. Practice race day nutrition and hydration strategy.

weeks.focusDescription: Peak week - highest volume before taper

days.cardioNotes: Easy conversational pace.
Recovery pace.
1 mile easy warm-up, 10 miles at marathon goal pace, 1 mile easy cool-down. Final marathon pace confidence builder.
Complete rest or easy cross-training
Final 20-miler. Nail your nutrition and pacing. You're ready for this. After today, the taper begins.

weeks.focusDescription: Begin taper - reduce volume while maintaining intensity

days.cardioNotes: Easy pace. Taper begins - enjoy the reduced mileage.
Recovery pace.
1 mile easy warm-up, 5 miles at marathon pace, 1 mile easy cool-down. Reduced volume but maintain race feel.
Last long run before race. Dial in race day routine and nutrition.

weeks.focusDescription: Deep taper - significant volume reduction while staying sharp

days.cardioNotes: Easy conversational pace. Keep legs fresh.
Recovery pace, stay loose.
1 mile easy, 3 miles at marathon pace, 1 mile easy. Keep the race pace feel sharp without fatigue.
Comfortable aerobic pace. Keep it short and easy.

weeks.focusDescription: Race week - minimal volume, maximum recovery, race day preparation

days.cardioNotes: Very easy pace. Just loosen up the legs.
Complete rest. Focus on hydration and nutrition.
Easy pace with 4-6 x 20-second strides at the end to stay sharp.
Complete rest. Prepare race gear and nutrition.
Very easy 2 miles. Nothing hard. Just movement to stay loose. Final check of legs before race day.
RACE DAY! You're ready. Trust your training. Start conservatively, execute your nutrition plan, and finish strong. Target: Sub-4:00 marathon (9:00-9:15/mile pace). Good luck!
